FSR-informed modification: The July 27, 2022 FOMC statement is distinctly hawkish. The Committee raised the target range to 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent, signaled “ongoing increases,” and continued balance-sheet runoff (Treasury caps rising to $60B/month and agency MBS to $35B/month in September). The Financial Stability Report (May 2022) reinforces this stance: it highlights upside inflation risks from Russia’s invasion of Ukraine via energy and commodity channels, broader price pressures beyond food and energy, and still-tight labor markets. While the FSR flags vulnerabilities (e.g., money market fund liquidity risks, market fragilities, elevated housing/asset valuations) that could be stressed by rapid tightening, these concerns only temper the tone at the margin; the dominant policy signal remains to lean aggressively against inflation. Net: hawkish with a nod to growth and stability risks.
